evidence.quote: | NetEndOfMonth days -> Json.objectOf [ "kind", Json.String "net-eom"; "days", number days ]
| true, days when days >= 1 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Every new rule is in Tier 1/2. The new terms variant, the due-date rule and the wording are in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The record codec is in Summa.Storage (Tier 2). The parsing and validation of the customer form's input are in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2). The change set touches no Tier 3 or Tier 4 code.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effects. The due date is computed purely from the issue date it is given; DateTime.DaysInMonth is a pure calendar function, not a clock read. The codec only builds and reads Json values in memory, and an Arca provider still does the persistence. The parser uses no I/O and does not read the clock.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The wording "Net N EOM" is written twice, once in Documents.termsText and once in Invoicing.termsWords for the audit trail. The two copies agree, and the code already did the same for Net N, but they are still a restated literal rather than one shared definition. The due-date rule and the net-eom storage kind each have a single definition.

evidence.quote: | true, day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The variant, the due-date rule and the ordinal wording are all in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The codec and its range check are in Summa.Storage (Tier 2), and the form parsing is in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2). The change set adds no Tier 3 or Tier 4 code.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effects. The due date is pure calendar arithmetic on the issue date it is given, and the codec and parser are pure functions. Persistence still goes through the existing provider.

evidence.quote: if day >= 1 && day <= 28 then Ok(DayOfNextMonth day)
| true, day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))
| DayOfNextMonth day -> $"Due the {dayOrdinal day} of next month"
| Some(DayOfNextMonth day) -> $"Due the {dayOrdinal day} of next month"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Two facts are copied, and in both cases the copies agree. First, the valid range of 1 to 28 is written in two places: in the Storage decoder and in the Engine form parser. Tier 1 has no single constructor or predicate that owns it, and Invoicing.dueDate itself does not guard it. Second, the sentence "Due the Nth of next month" is written in both Documents.termsText and Invoicing.termsWords. The ordinal suffix itself is defined once, in dayOrdinal, and both copies use it.
